To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the atmospheric neutrinos in multi-GeV range are sensitive to small θ13 and that the matter effects can lead to an observable asymmetry of the electron neutrinos with respect to the updown direction of the earth.
the oscillations of muon neutrinos into sterile neutrinos in the Earth can be enhanced due to the MSW and the parametric resonance effects.

the oscillations of the multi-TeV atmospheric neutrinos can be enhanced by the parametric resonance in the subdominat mode νμ ↔ ν3 and that the resonance matter effects lead an observable zenith angle dependence of the up-down asymmetry of the electron-like events.

the super-Kamioka data are consistent with νμ → ντ oscillations in the range 1 × 10−2 eV2 ≤ ∆m2 ≤ 1 × 103 eV2 and 0 ≤ sin2 2Θ ≤ 1.
the data are in good agreement with the oscillations of the subdominant neutrino component in the νμ ↔ ντ channel.
the atmospheric neutrino anomaly is most probably due to νμ ↔ ντ oscillations with Δm2 ∝ (0.5–3) × 103eV2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atmospheric neutrino data are compatible with the three-neutrinos scheme with the large mixing angle θ13 ∼ 0.3 and Δm2 ∽ (1–2.5) × 10-3 eV2.
the MSW resonance in the νμ → νe channel is not necessary for the explanation of the super-K data, and that the parametric resonance can explain the data even in the absence of the MSW resonance.
the MSW resonance in the νμ ↔ ντ mode can be used to determine the mass hierarchy and the parametric resonance in the νµ ↔ νe mode can be used as an independent test of the mass hierarchy.
